text:
maya: Heads-up: we just got multiple customer tickets about 5xx/timeouts from hosted inference since ~07:12 UTC. Customers report intermittent 502/504 and long tail latencies (~10-30s). Root request IDs: r-01F4Z2X, r-01F4Z9P. Attaching a sample reply from the API gateway:

maya: sample curl that customer ran:
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-XXXX" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-4-redwood","input":"hello"}' \
  https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
Content-Type: application/json
{"error":{"type":"upstream_error","message":"kv-cache upstream timeout"}}
```

maya: Customers are escalated, some have timed out client-side. Not a billing issue; they can reproduce on fresh tokens. Any ideas? @jin @priya @diego

jin: Oncall - looking. I'm seeing a surge of connection timeouts to our prefix-caching service (redis read replicas). Metrics: connection_errors spiked at 07:10 UTC and P99 latency for GETs went from 8ms -> 1.2s. Some replicas flipped to readonly; cluster reports partial failover.

redis-alerts: ALERT: redis-prefix-cache latency > 800ms (instances: cache-prod-1, cache-prod-3). Error rate increased 14x.

priya: Thanks. Which API routes hit the prefix cache? Is this embeddings prefix caching or chat session KV cache?

maya: Mostly /v1/generate (chat + completion routes) and some rerank. Customers mention degraded streaming as well.

diego: Quick triage: the runtime tries to read prefix KV for cache hits before calling model. If KV times out we currently do a synchronous fallback path that retries and can block the request for a long time -> leads to gateway 504s when overall request exceeds upstream timeout.

priya: OK. Short-term mitigation: we can flip the feature flag to bypass prefix caching for hosted tier (config scope: runtime.cache.prefix_enabled = false) which will avoid hitting redis entirely and fall back to model call. That will increase token costs but restore availability.

alex: Customer asked for ETA; can we do that toggle as tenant-specific override so enterprise customers keep caching? They want minimal impact to throughput.

jin: I can do a global toggle first to stop the pain, then re-enable per-tenant after cluster stabilizes. Rolling global toggle via /admin/config API should be instant.

priya: Also: runtime patch ready to be canaried — change behavior to async-prefetch with a short 60ms deadline and local in-memory fallback for missed prefixes. I can push a 5% canary to hosted region eu-west-1. Should reduce blocking.

maya: Steps to reproduce (customer repro):
1) Send /v1/generate with long system prompt and streaming enabled.
2) Repeat with ~10 concurrent connections using same session id -> server will attempt prefix lookup and sometimes hit the slow path.

maya: exact repro curl (customer):
```
for i in {1..10}; do \
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-XXXX" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\
    -d '{"model":"gpt-4-redwood","input":"<long-system-prompt>","stream":true,"session_id":"acct-123"}' \\
    https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate &
 done; wait
```

diego: Jin, can you check the cache-proxy pods (cache-proxy-*) and redis replicas? I'll prepare the config toggle command.

jin: Actions I'm taking now:
- Restarting cache-proxy pods in us-east-1 (rolling)
- Evicting a stuck replica (cache-redis-03) and forcing a failover to warm standby
- Increasing maxclients and connection pool size temporarily

jin: logs from cache-proxy just before restart:
```
[2026-03-15T07:09:58Z] WARN upstream_get failed: dial tcp 10.2.3.45:6379: i/o timeout
[2026-03-15T07:10:03Z] ERROR prefix_lookup timeout after 1200ms for key tenant:acct-123:prefix-0
```

redis-alerts: INFO: redis cluster reported replica promotion for cache-redis-04 -> master at 07:16 UTC.

priya: I'm going to roll the config toggle now (runtime.cache.prefix_enabled=false) at the global level, and start the canary patch in parallel. Diego, can you coordinate a post-toggle note to customers?

diego: Doing toggle now via admin API (command):
```
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer admin-YYYY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  https://console.internal.redwood/v1/admin/config \
  -d '{"runtime.cache.prefix_enabled":false}'
```

diego: Toggle executed at 07:20 UTC. Confirmed runtime config polls applied to hosted nodes within 30s.

maya: Reporting: customers seeing immediate improvement in success rate (one customer confirmed streaming restored). Still monitoring for edge cases.

jin: After evict and restart, redis P95 read latency back to ~12ms and connection errors dropped. I also scaled redis-read-replicas from 3 -> 5 to handle spike.

priya: Canary patch (async-prefetch + 60ms deadline) deployed to 5% and is healthy. Telemetry shows failed prefix reads now degrade locally without blocking main model call. Throughput normalized.

alex: Customer-facing summary I sent: "We identified a transient outage in our prefix-caching layer (Redis) that increased read latencies and led to gateway timeouts. We've temporarily disabled prefix caching for hosted production to restore service and applied patches to make prefix reads non-blocking. We're investigating root cause and will follow up with remediation and postmortem." They appreciated ETA and that billing unaffected.

maya: Action items for postmortem / follow-ups:
- jin: run deeper analysis on disk/memory contention and network flaps for cache-redis-03 (investigate why replica went readonly)
- priya: make async-prefetch + short deadline the default and add per-tenant toggles in Console UI
- eng-sre: add circuit-breaker metric and alert for prefix-cache timeouts > 200ms
- runtime: add per-request trace tag when fallback used so we can correlate customer tickets

jin: Will open incident ticket and link redis logs & perf profiles.

priya: Also recommend adding a graceful degradation knob that falls back to memcached/local-LRU when redis cluster is unhealthy.

maya: Thanks everyone. Marking thread resolved for now — I'll update customers once postmortem draft ready. :thumbsup:

alex: One customer follow-up asked for exact start/end times for SLA credit — maya, can you attach logs/times to the ticket once you have them.

maya: Will do. Closing thread but leaving incident doc link in ticket when available.
